```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  message = FALSE,

```

# Problem 1

```{r load-noaa}
data("ny_noaa")

noaa_missing =
  ny_noaa |>
  summarize(across(everything(), ~ mean(is.na(.x)))) |>
  pivot_longer(
    everything(),
    names_to = "variable",
    values_to = "missing_proportion"
  )

knitr::kable(noaa_missing, digits = 3)
```

The original dataset contains `r nrow(ny_noaa)` observations and
`r ncol(ny_noaa)` variables. Each row records weather measurements
for a station on a particular date. Key variables include station ID,
date, precipitation, snowfall, snow depth, and minimum and maximum
temperature. The table above shows the proportion of missing values
for each variable.

```{r clean-noaa}
noaa =
  ny_noaa |>
  mutate(
    year = as.integer(format(date, "%Y")),
    month = as.integer(format(date, "%m")),
    day = as.integer(format(date, "%d")),
    prcp = prcp / 10,
    tmax = as.numeric(tmax) / 10,
    tmin = as.numeric(tmin) / 10
  )

snowfall_counts =
  noaa |>
  filter(!is.na(snow)) |>
  count(snow, sort = TRUE) |>
  slice_head(n = 10)

knitr::kable(
  snowfall_counts,
  col.names = c("Snowfall (mm)", "Number of observations")
)
```

Precipitation is expressed in millimeters and temperature in degrees
Celsius. Snowfall and snow depth remain in millimeters. Zero snowfall
is common because most days have no measurable snowfall. Repeated
positive values may reflect measurements originally recorded in inches
and converted to millimeters.

```{r noaa-monthly-temperatures}
station_temperature =
  noaa |>
  filter(month %in% c(1, 7)) |>
  group_by(id, year, month) |>
  summarize(
    mean_tmax = mean(tmax, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(is.finite(mean_tmax)) |>
  mutate(
    month = factor(
      month,
      levels = c(1, 7),
      labels = c("January", "July")
    )
  )

ggplot(
  station_temperature,
  aes(x = year, y = mean_tmax, group = id)
) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.15, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.15, size = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ month, nrow = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Average maximum temperature by station and year",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Average maximum temperature (°C)"
  )
```

```{r noaa-temperature-snowfall, fig.width=12, fig.height=6}
temperature_plot =
  noaa |>
  filter(!is.na(tmin), !is.na(tmax)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, y = tmax)) +
  geom_hex(bins = 60) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(trans = "log10") +
  labs(
    title = "Maximum versus minimum temperature",
    x = "Minimum temperature (°C)",
    y = "Maximum temperature (°C)",
    fill = "Count"
  )

snowfall_plot =
  noaa |>
  filter(snow > 0, snow < 100) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(year), y = snow)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.alpha = 0.1) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of snowfall by year",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Snowfall (mm)"
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 90,
      hjust = 1,
      size = 7
    )
  )

temperature_plot + snowfall_plot
```

# Problem 2

```{r clean-nhanes}
nhanes_covar =
  read_csv(
    "data/nhanes_covar.csv",
    skip = 4,
    na = c("", "NA", ".")
  ) |>
  clean_names() |>
  drop_na() |>
  filter(age >= 21) |>
  mutate(
    sex = factor(
      sex,
      levels = c(1, 2),
      labels = c("Male", "Female")
    ),
    education = factor(
      education,
      levels = c(1, 2, 3),
      labels = c(
        "Less than high school",
        "High school equivalent",
        "More than high school"
      )
    )
  )

nhanes_accel =
  read_csv("data/nhanes_accel.csv") |>
  clean_names() |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("min"),
    names_to = "minute",
    names_prefix = "min",
    names_transform = list(minute = as.integer),
    values_to = "mims"
  )

nhanes =
  inner_join(
    nhanes_covar,
    nhanes_accel,
    by = "seqn"
  ) |>
  mutate(hour = (minute - 1) / 60)
```

After excluding participants younger than 21 years and those with
missing demographic information, the dataset includes
`r n_distinct(nhanes$seqn)` participants. Each row in the long dataset
represents one participant's activity during one minute. Demographic
variables include sex, age, BMI, and education.

```{r nhanes-demographic-table}
education_sex_table =
  nhanes_covar |>
  count(education, sex) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = sex,
    values_from = n,
    values_fill = 0
  )

knitr::kable(
  education_sex_table,
  col.names = c("Education", "Male", "Female"),
  caption = "Participant counts by education and sex"
)
```

```{r nhanes-age-distribution}
ggplot(
  nhanes_covar,
  aes(x = sex, y = age, fill = sex)
) +
  geom_violin(alpha = 0.5, trim = FALSE) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.15, outlier.shape = NA) +
  facet_wrap(~ education, nrow = 1) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  labs(
    title = "Age distribution by sex and education",
    x = "Sex",
    y = "Age (years)"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

The sample contains 228 eligible participants. The group with more than
a high school education has the most participants. Men and women have
similar counts in the lowest and highest education categories, while
the high school equivalent category contains more men than women.

```{r nhanes-total-activity}
daily_activity =
  nhanes |>
  group_by(seqn, sex, age, bmi, education) |>
  summarize(
    observed_minutes = sum(!is.na(mims)),
    total_activity = if_else(
      observed_minutes == 1440L,
      sum(mims, na.rm = TRUE),
      NA_real_
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(
  daily_activity,
  aes(x = age, y = total_activity, color = sex)
) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ education, nrow = 1) +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
  labs(
    title = "Total daily activity by age, sex, and education",
    x = "Age (years)",
    y = "Total daily activity (MIMS)",
    color = "Sex"
  )
```

```{r nhanes-activity-timecourse}
activity_timecourse =
  nhanes |>
  group_by(education, sex, minute, hour) |>
  summarize(
    mean_mims = mean(mims, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(
  activity_timecourse,
  aes(x = hour, y = mean_mims, color = sex)
) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.25, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "loess",
    span = 0.15,
    se = FALSE,
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ education, nrow = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, 24, 6),
    limits = c(0, 24)
  ) +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
  labs(
    title = "Average activity throughout the day",
    x = "Hour of day",
    y = "Mean activity (MIMS)",
    color = "Sex"
  )
```

# Problem 3

```{r clean-citibike}
jan_2020 =
  read_csv("data/citibike/Jan 2020 Citi.csv") |>
  mutate(year = 2020L, month = "January")

july_2020 =
  read_csv("data/citibike/July 2020 Citi.csv") |>
  mutate(year = 2020L, month = "July")

jan_2024 =
  read_csv("data/citibike/Jan 2024 Citi.csv") |>
  mutate(year = 2024L, month = "January")

july_2024 =
  read_csv("data/citibike/July 2024 Citi.csv") |>
  mutate(year = 2024L, month = "July")

citibike =
  bind_rows(jan_2020, july_2020, jan_2024, july_2024) |>
  clean_names() |>
  mutate(
    year = factor(year),
    month = factor(month, levels = c("January", "July")),
    weekdays = factor(
      weekdays,
      levels = c(
        "Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday", "Thursday",
        "Friday", "Saturday", "Sunday"
      )
    ),
    member_casual = factor(
      member_casual,
      levels = c("casual", "member"),
      labels = c("Casual", "Member")
    ),
    rideable_type = factor(
      rideable_type,
      levels = c("classic_bike", "electric_bike"),
      labels = c("Classic bike", "Electric bike")
    )
  )

glimpse(citibike)
```

The combined dataset contains `r nrow(citibike)` rides and
`r ncol(citibike)` variables. Variables include ride ID, bike type,
day of the week, ride duration in minutes, starting and ending station,
membership status, year, and month. These data are samples of rides,
rather than all Citi Bike rides.

```{r citibike-ride-counts}
ride_counts =
  citibike |>
  count(year, month, member_casual) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = member_casual,
    values_from = n,
    values_fill = 0
  ) |>
  arrange(year, month)

knitr::kable(
  ride_counts,
  col.names = c("Year", "Month", "Casual", "Member"),
  format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
  caption = "Number of sampled rides by year, month, and membership"
)
```

Members account for more rides than casual riders in every year-month
combination. July has more rides than January in both years. The
sample also contains more rides in 2024 than in the corresponding
months of 2020.

```{r citibike-top-stations}
top_stations =
  citibike |>
  filter(year == "2024", month == "July") |>
  filter(!is.na(start_station_name)) |>
  count(start_station_name, sort = TRUE) |>
  slice_head(n = 5)

knitr::kable(
  top_stations,
  col.names = c("Starting station", "Number of rides"),
  caption = "Five most popular starting stations in July 2024"
)
```

```{r citibike-median-duration}
median_duration =
  citibike |>
  group_by(year, month, weekdays) |>
  summarize(
    median_duration = median(duration, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(
  median_duration,
  aes(
    x = weekdays,
    y = median_duration,
    color = month,
    group = month
  )
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~ year, nrow = 1) +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
  labs(
    title = "Median ride duration by weekday, month, and year",
    x = "Day of the week",
    y = "Median ride duration (minutes)",
    color = "Month"
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
  )
```

```{r citibike-2024-duration}
citibike |>
  filter(year == "2024") |>
  ggplot(
    aes(
      x = member_casual,
      y = duration,
      fill = rideable_type
    )
  ) +
  geom_boxplot(
    outlier.alpha = 0.1,
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ month, nrow = 1) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  labs(
    title = "Ride duration distributions in 2024",
    x = "Membership status",
    y = "Ride duration (minutes, log scale)",
    fill = "Bike type"
  )
```
